harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed AIDE on node1 and established a full checksum-based integrity baseline covering /etc (via the Ubuntu aide-common config's catch-all Full rule plus package-specific rules). Verified detection works by modifying /etc/hosts.allow and observing AIDE report the exact MD5/SHA1/SHA256/SHA512/etc. diffs, then reverted the change and refreshed the baseline to a clean state. Confirmed the built-in dailyaidecheck.timer is enabled/active for ongoing scheduled integrity reporting. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot ID and aide.db checksum, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot ID changed (proving an actual restart, not just elapsed time), and ran a fresh AIDE check post-restart showing the aide.db persisted unchanged and zero /etc entries differed (all 428 diffs were confined to volatile /var, /run, /tmp paths from the reboot itself, none in /etc).
actions_performed: Checked OS and confirmed AIDE not preinstalled on node1
Installed aide + aide-common packages
Inspected /etc/aide/aide.conf and aide.conf.d rule structure, confirming /etc is covered by the catch-all Full (checksummed) rule plus dedicated per-package /etc rules
Initialized the AIDE database (aide --init), producing 87,378 baselined entries
Activated the baseline by copying aide.db.new to aide.db
Ran aide --check confirming zero real differences (only my own /tmp scratch files and a transient /run entry)
Modified /etc/hosts.allow as a live detection test and reran aide --check, confirming AIDE reported the exact file with full multi-algorithm checksum diffs
Reverted the test change, confirmed content checksums matched baseline again post-revert (only inode/mtime metadata differed from the edit)
Ran aide --update and activated the refreshed clean baseline
Confirmed dailyaidecheck.timer is enabled and active for ongoing scheduled reporting
Captured pre-restart boot ID and aide.db checksum
Issued systemctl reboot on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again post-reboot
Confirmed boot ID changed and aide.db persisted with identical checksum, timer re-active
Ran post-restart aide --check and confirmed zero /etc-path entries in the diff, verifying /etc integrity baseline survived the restart untouched

evidence.requirement: Establish an AIDE integrity baseline for /etc on node1
evidence.summary: AIDE installed; /etc coverage confirmed via config; database initialized (87,378 entries) and activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db

evidence.requirement: Baseline is clean/accurate immediately after creation
evidence.summary: aide --check on the fresh baseline reported 0 changed entries; only unrelated /tmp scratch files and one /run entry appeared as added/removed, nothing in /etc

evidence.requirement: Baseline enables identifying/reporting later changes to /etc files
evidence.summary: Live test: modified /etc/hosts.allow, then aide --check reported the exact file with full MD5/SHA1/SHA256/SHA512/etc. before/after checksums, proving change detection works

evidence.requirement: Baseline restored to accurate clean state after test
evidence.summary: Test change reverted; verified content checksums matched (only inode/mtime differed); ran aide --update and activated the refreshed clean database

evidence.requirement: Ongoing periodic integrity reporting mechanism present
evidence.summary: systemctl shows dailyaidecheck.timer enabled and active, scheduled to trigger the daily AIDE check/report

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (29011044-...), aide.db sha256 checksum, and confirmed dailyaidecheck.timer enabled/active

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns, restart executes
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background with nohup/disown; command returned (stream closed as node went down) confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: Node unreachable immediately after reboot; polling succeeded with uptime '0 min'; new boot_id 94827432-... differs from pre-restart 29011044-..., proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: required data/service recovery verified
evidence.summary: Post-restart: aide.db checksum identical to pre-restart (data persisted), dailyaidecheck.timer active again, and a full aide --check showed zero changed/added/removed entries under /etc (all 428 diffs confined to volatile /var, /run, /tmp paths from the reboot itself)
